acceptance_evidence.acceptance_criterion: 重复执行收敛到同一 durable result (re-execution converges to the same durable result)
acceptance_evidence.mandatory_test_1_retry_same_operation: p4t2-journal.test.ts 'retry same operation (mandatory)': re-execute + re-drive of a committed operation return the identical durable result (phase/idempotencyKey/canonical-intent JSON/childSessionId/ledgerSequence byte-identical via serializeOperationRecord and durableOutcomeShape), perform ZERO writes, and the ledger keeps exactly one fact (seq 1) with no gaps; raw store keys stay [op-row, '1', counter].
acceptance_evidence.mandatory_test_2_generation_conflict: p4t2-conflicts.test.ts 'generation CAS (mandatory)': expectedGeneration 1 vs committed gen 2 -> stale-generation (RECORD_INVALID, expected/found); drive with stale expectedGeneration fails identically; expectedGeneration 1 on a fresh (absent) operation fails with found:null; expectedGeneration 0 (expect-absent) is the CAS that admits first prepare; matching expectedGeneration drives clean; every conflict path performs zero writes. Engine rule: an absent row satisfies expectedGeneration 0 (verifyGeneration normalizes found===null to 0).
acceptance_evidence.mandatory_test_3_duplicate_ledger_preven: p4t2-conflicts.test.ts 'duplicate ledger prevention (mandatory)': three committed operations in one world yield exactly three facts (one per operationId), sequences [1,2,3] with gaps [], raw ledger keys exactly ['1','2','3','__ledger_sequence_counter'], and the first fact's raw bytes are byte-stable across all later drives/conflicts (no re-allocation, no rewrite). Crash side: p4t2-crash-recovery.test.ts scenario F proves that when the fact is durable but the COMMITTED put is not, recovery REUSES the allocated sequence (fact 7) instead of allocating a duplicate; scenario D/E prove counter-gap behavior (allocated-but-lost sequence 5 becomes a permanent gap, later facts 6/7/8 continue — no sequence reuse).
acceptance_evidence.crash_recovery: p4t2-crash-recovery.test.ts: crash armed after each of the 7 writes of a fresh operation (k=0..5) plus a staged prepare->recordChildSession crash (G); every recovery completes to the SAME durable result (semantic outcome identical to the no-crash run), re-applies effects idempotently (applied/skipped split matches what the crash already persisted), writes nothing for an already-converged operation, and the whole run issues ZERO deletes. Final world: 7 facts, sequences [1,2,3,4,6,7,8], gaps [5], every target record written exactly once.
acceptance_evidence.protocol_never_rolls_back: All three test files carry a global no-delete assertion over every seam's writeLog (entry.op !== 'delete'); recovery is roll-forward/reconcile only (DevPlan §17.3).
acceptance_evidence.cross_team: p4t2-conflicts.test.ts 'cross-team fact conflict' + p4t2-journal.test.ts world A root-2 journal: the operations store is global (frozen v1 OperationRecord has no team field) while the journal is team-scoped; a foreign team's journal cannot serve, re-drive, or read the sequence of an operation committed under another root — execute/drive reject with idempotency-conflict (expected/found roots) and lastApplied()/factSequence() see nothing. Engine fix exercised by this test: driveRow now performs the foreign-fact scope check BEFORE the terminal short-circuit, matching execute.

notes.p4_t1_defect_findings: none — all 564 P4-T1 baseline tests pass unmodified; P4-T1 repository/seam behavior matched the documented contract everywhere P4-T2 exercises it (idempotent puts, typed conflicts, ledger counter boot/allocate, seam crash fake). No P4-T1 code was touched.
interpretations: (a) lastAppliedOperationId: the frozen v1 DTOs carry no lastAppliedOperationId field (grep-verified across contracts v1), so its durable carrier is the ledger fact's operationId link (factType payload + operationId on the fact row). journal.lastApplied(team) returns the operationId of the highest-sequence fact of the bound team's ledger that links an operation; journal.factSequence(operationId) returns that fact's sequence (or rejects with idempotency-conflict when the fact belongs to another team). Documented in packages/storage/operations/journal.ts header.

(b) Convergence semantics: 'same durable result' means the semantic outcome is stable across crash/attempt history — phase, idempotency key, canonical intent bytes, child session, effects-applied-once, and a single ledger fact with stable bytes. Wall-clock updatedAt, row generation, and sequence numbers after lost-allocations (gaps) are legitimately attempt-dependent audit/bookkeeping and are excluded from the durable-outcome comparison (documented in p4t2-helpers.durableOutcomeShape and the journal.ts header).

(c) Journal is TEAM-scoped (bound rootSessionId) while the operations store is GLOBAL (frozen v1 OperationRecord has no team field); same-operationId collisions across teams surface as idempotency-conflict on the foreign fact rather than silent cross-team convergence.

(d) The per-operationId lock is a process-local complement to the domain write chain (serialize-within-domain per Arch §14.4); it provides no cross-process guarantee, which the domain seam's write serialization owns.

(e) Write budget (measured, InMemoryStorageSeam): domain bootstrap stamps 8 schema_meta rows on first open; fresh operation = 7 writes (prepare, binding, member, counter boot+update = 2, fact, COMMITTED put); later operations = 5-6 writes depending on effect skip; retry/re-drive of a converged operation = 0 writes. A crashed fact allocation leaves a permanent ledger gap (sequences are never reused).
